FIX: sessionEnd.ts watchStoredPrincipal(scope) remembers the stored boe.<scope>.principal at restore start; anotherUserSince(userId) re-reads it and is true only when it changed since the start (or since the restore's own last write, tracked by wrote()) and names a different, parsable user than the server's answer; null and unparsable values are ignored. Client cookieRestore: checked before storing getClientWebCsrf's user. Admin cookieRestore: checked before storing getWebCsrf's user (then wrote() records that write) and again before storing getAdminSession's user. On true: nothing is written, endSession('revoked') (compare-and-delete keeps the other user's stored principal and CSRF), restore resolves null; SessionProvider keeps the reason, so sign-in shows 'Your session was ended for security'; a reload restores as the other user. Native restores unchanged (cookieRestore is web only).

Left as is, deliberately: cookieSignIn (both shells) still writes over another user's stored principal, because a sign-in in this tab sets this browser's cookies to that user, so its principal is the truth and other tabs end via the listener. executeCookieRefresh's write is not the same class: POST /v1/auth/web/refresh sets the rotated cookies in its own response (webAuthRoutes.ts applyAuthCookies), while GET csrf and GET session set none, so a refresh writes what its own cookies say.

Exempt: unauthenticated:true, and contract authChannel 'public' or 'public-token' (read from the operation descriptor; no operation ids). Re-checked on every GET retry attempt.

N1: on a 401 (any code) when the tab no longer holds the sender -> rethrow, no refresh, no endSession, so the first end's reason stands. N2: after refreshOnce, if the tab no longer holds the sender -> rethrow original error, no resend and no end (covers native and the non-rotated outcomes too; rule 15).

N3: new src/api/session/sessionEnd.ts: endSession(tokenStore, scope, reason) (moved out of http.ts) and endSessionOnOtherTabSignIn(scope, tokenStore): a 'storage' listener on boe.<scope>.principal; ignores other keys, removals, unparsable values, same userId, and a tab holding no user; otherwise ends with reason 'revoked' (existing copy 'Your session was ended for security'). Wired in SessionProvider only while a principal is signed in.

Why SessionProvider and not the runtime: createAdminRuntime/createClientRuntime are also built ad hoc by probeReachability (a runtime-level listener would leak), and a signed-out web tab hydrates a stale principal from localStorage, so a runtime listener would flash the security notice on a sign-in screen.
Native: no cross-tab storage (one WebView document, secure storage); the listener is inert there and native behaviour is unchanged.

tokenStore.clear FINDING: before, clear removed all four persisted keys; on web principal and csrfToken live in shared localStorage, so tab A's end (storage-event end, replaced end, sign-out) deleted B's principal and CSRF token written by B's tab. Harm found: none functional (B's tab reads memory; its reload restores from cookies via getWebCsrf/getClientWebCsrf; the removal event is ignored). Fixed for the class anyway: secrets are removed immediately as before; principal/csrfToken are removed only if the persisted value still equals what this tab held and this tab has not stored a new one since (compare-and-delete, async after a read).

Bootstrap fix: client nativeRestore now returns null when the cached principal has no readable userId (otherwise the APK would be signed in while the guard refuses every request with no end). Principal has carried userId since a1894c8, so this is defensive.

F1 subscribe-time check (sessionEnd.ts): endSessionOnOtherTabSignIn now reads localStorage boe.<scope>.principal once when it subscribes and applies the listener's rule (ignore no value, unparsable value, same userId, a tab holding no user; otherwise endSession 'revoked'). Both the listener and the check are skipped on native (isNative), so native is unchanged.

F1 admin case: the subscribe check alone does NOT end a switch between getWebCsrf and getAdminSession, because cookieRestore overwrote the held principal with getAdminSession's user (tab held B, stored B, no mismatch; it kept A's CSRF token). Fix: cookieRestore compares getAdminSession's userId with the user getWebCsrf just stored; on a mismatch endSession('revoked') and resolve null. SessionProvider now keeps the endedReason announced during the restore when the restore resolves null, so the sign-in shows 'Your session was ended for security'. A switch after getAdminSession is caught by the subscribe check or the listener.

F2 (adminRuntime.ts, clientRuntime.ts): a web cookie restore that resolves signed out now clears the scope: any getWebCsrf/getClientWebCsrf failure (catch -> clear -> null), and a non-outage getAdminSession error (clear, then rethrow as before). A getAdminSession outage (isOutage: timeout, offline or status >= 500) does not clear and still throws, so SessionProvider stays 'restoring' with the retry and the tab restores when the network returns.

Outage classification today, checked: getWebCsrf/getClientWebCsrf failures of every kind, outage included, already resolved signed out (sign-in screen) before this lane; only the admin getAdminSession outage throws. I kept that classification (rethrowing a CSRF-recovery outage would leave deep links on RequireSession's endless 'Restoring your session' spinner, which has no retry). Clearing there is safe for restoring later: web restores re-read the user from cookies and web persists no secrets.

Compare-and-delete confirmed (STATIC + round-3 RC6): on a signed-out restore the held values are the hydrated copies; a value another tab wrote after the load differs and is kept; an unchanged one is removed, and since the restore just found no cookie session no live tab of that origin is using it (tabs read memory, reloads read cookies).
